chief_complaint: watery tearing, severe burning, redness, and tender preauricular lymph node starting in one eye and spreading to both
hpi_details: 29M post-URI presenting with watery discharge, follicular conjunctival reaction, and tender palpable preauricular lymphadenopathy caused by highly contagious Adenovirus managed with supportive artificial tears and strict handwashing without antibiotics.
ideas: He thinks the head cold he had last week spread into his sinuses and travelled into his tear ducts.
concerns: He is worried that the tender lump in front of his ear is a tumor or a deep salivary gland infection that might require surgery.
expectations: He hopes to be prescribed strong eye drops to soothe the burning and to have the doctor examine the lump near his ear.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis / epidemic keratoconjunctivitis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis / epidemic keratoconjunctivitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis / epidemic keratoconjunctivitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial conjunctivitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Highly contagious — spread precautions needed.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Viral Conjunctivitis Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Viral Conjunctivitis Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis.
reference_soap.plan: Provide supportive care with preservative-free artificial tears and cool compresses; routine antibiotics are not indicated. Reinforce hand hygiene, avoidance of shared towels/cosmetics, and avoidance of contact lenses until resolved. Arrange ophthalmology assessment for pain, photophobia, reduced vision, corneal findings, or prolonged/severe symptoms.

must_ask.objective: Ask about recent upper respiratory infection

history.answer: My eyes are bright red, watery, and burning really badly.
It started about three days ago in my right eye, and then yesterday morning my left eye became red and started tearing up as well.
The redness is all over the white parts of both eyes, not just in one isolated spot or around the colored iris.
It feels like a severe burning and stinging sensation with a gritty, sandy feeling, but there is no deep throbbing ache inside my eyes.
My eyesight is normal, though my vision can blur slightly for a second when tears build up until I blink.
Bright light is slightly bothersome because my eyes are irritated, but looking at light does not cause sharp or deep eye pain.
No, I have not seen any rainbow rings or halos around lights, and I have no headache, nausea, or vomiting.
The drainage is completely watery and clear. When I wake up my eyelids are slightly crusty and stuck, but there is no thick yellow or green pus.
No, my eyes are not itchy at all; they mostly burn and water.
My eyelids look a bit puffy from the irritation, but I do not have any painful bumps or crusting along the lashes.
Moving my eyes does not hurt at all, my eyes are not bulging, I do not see double, and I do not have a fever.
I had a mild cold with a sore throat and runny nose about five days ago, and a colleague at work had red eyes last week.
No, I do not wear contact lenses at all.
No, I have not had any injury or hit to my eyes, no dust or chemicals splashed in, and I have not been exposed to welding light.
No, this has never happened seasonally, and I do not have seasonal allergies, hay fever, asthma, or eczema.
I work on a computer for my job, but my eyes have never felt unusually dry before this, and I do not have dry mouth.
No, I do not have morning lower back stiffness, joint swelling, painful mouth ulcers, or stomach trouble.
No, I have never had cold sores, blisters on my face, forehead, or tip of my nose, or any previous herpes infections.
No, I am not taking aspirin or blood thinners, and I have not had any severe bouts of coughing, vomiting, or heavy straining.
No, I have never had glaucoma, eye surgery, or any eye disease before this episode.
Yes, I noticed a tender, swollen little lump right in front of my right ear that hurts whenever I touch it.
I had a bad cold last week, so I thought the virus must have traveled up into my sinuses and into my eyes.
The painful bump right by my ear really scares me—I'm worried it might be a swollen tumor or a gland that needs to be cut out.
I have high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol, but no other medical problems.
I have never had any surgeries or been hospitalized.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day for my blood pressure, and I have not used any eye drops yet.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I do not smoke cigarettes and have never smoked.
I only drink socially, maybe one or two beers once a month.
I work as an office accountant and live in an apartment with my wife.
My father has high blood pressure, but there is no family history of glaucoma, vision loss, or autoimmune diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable young male in no acute distress, with prominent bilateral conjunctival redness and watery tearing.
Diffuse bilateral conjunctival injection with prominent follicular reaction on the inferior palpebral conjunctiva and watery tearing, with no subconjunctival hemorrhage or jaundice.

Visual acuity is 20/20 bilaterally, pupils are equal and briskly reactive, extraocular movements are full without diplopia, corneas are clear without fluorescein uptake, and eversion reveals no foreign bodies.
A tender, palpable right preauricular lymph node is present, with no other cervical lymphadenopathy.
Mild nasal mucosal erythema without discharge; pharynx is clear without tonsillar exudates.
